frameworks.justification: This framework organizes findings by distinguishing between studies focused on instrument development and those examining psychological constructs, reflecting the dominant analytical axis of measurement focus vs. psychological constructs.
frameworks.general_objective: To systematically analyze the distribution and integration of psychometric instrument development and psychological construct assessment in engineering education research.

specific_objectives.text: Evaluate the scope and robustness of instrument development and validation methods across major competency and psychological construct domains.
key_themes: Instrument Development, Validation, and Psychometric Analysis

specific_objectives.text: Compare the prevalence and measurement approaches for self-efficacy, attitudes, and demographic influences versus identity, motivation, and persistence.
key_themes: Identity, Motivation, and Persistence in Engineering

specific_objectives.text: Assess the integration of reflective thinking and decision-making constructs within broader psychometric frameworks.
key_themes: Instrument Development, Validation, and Psychometric Analysis

specific_objectives.text: Examine how internship and work experience evaluation instruments complement psychological construct assessments.

strengths: Clear distinction between tool development and construct measurement
Facilitates identification of gaps in construct coverage
limitations: May underrepresent contextual factors like internships
Limited integration of reflective thinking due to low study count

frameworks.justification: This framework leverages the individual vs. contextual factors and competency breadth vs. depth axes to organize studies by internal attributes, external influences, and competency specificity.
frameworks.general_objective: To investigate how individual psychological attributes and contextual factors interact across broad and specialized competency assessments in engineering education.

specific_objectives.text: Analyze the relationship between self-efficacy, attitudes, and demographic influences (individual factors) and identity, motivation, and persistence.
key_themes: Identity, Motivation, and Persistence in Engineering

specific_objectives.text: Compare the assessment of broad transversal skills versus specialized competencies and mindsets, including their psychometric foundations.
key_themes: Instrument Development, Validation, and Psychometric Analysis

specific_objectives.text: Evaluate the role of contextual factors (internships, work experience, COVID-19) in shaping self-efficacy and competency development.
Examine how reflective thinking and decision-making competencies are assessed in relation to individual and contextual factors.

strengths: Reveals gaps in contextual factor integration
limitations: Lower coverage due to exclusion of pure instrument development studies
Limited studies on reflective thinking reduce relational analysis robustness

frameworks.approach: Competency Domain and Psychometric Integration Framework
frameworks.justification: This framework organizes findings by competency domains (psychological constructs, specialized skills, reflective processes) and their psychometric underpinnings, emphasizing the strong associations between instrument development and construct assessment.
frameworks.general_objective: To synthesize the psychometric validation of competency assessments across psychological, specialized, and reflective domains in engineering education.

specific_objectives.text: Map the psychometric properties and validation methods used for self-efficacy, attitudes, and demographic influence instruments.
key_themes: Instrument Development, Validation, and Psychometric Analysis

specific_objectives.text: Assess the psychometric quality and domain coverage of specialized competency and mindset assessment tools.
key_themes: Instrument Development, Validation, and Psychometric Analysis

specific_objectives.text: Investigate the psychometric integration of identity, motivation, and persistence measures with competency assessments.
key_themes: Identity, Motivation, and Persistence in Engineering

specific_objectives.text: Evaluate the psychometric foundations of reflective thinking and decision-making instruments in engineering contexts.
key_themes: Instrument Development, Validation, and Psychometric Analysis

strengths: Strong focus on psychometric rigor across domains
High coverage due to central role of instrument development
limitations: May overlook contextual factors like internships
Low study count for reflective thinking limits depth
Less emphasis on demographic and contextual influences

data.recommendation: I recommend the Psychometric and Construct Coverage Framework because it provides the highest coverage (95%) of the data, directly aligns with the dominant analytical axis (measurement focus vs. psychological constructs), and leverages the strongest empirical relationships (e.g., instrument development with self-efficacy and specialized competencies). It also allows for comparative and relational analyses across all major themes, including the smaller but relevant internship and reflective thinking areas, while maintaining a clear organizational logic grounded in the inductive findings.
